picks.title: Poetry Unbound in Conversation — Haleh Liza Gafori
picks.summary: Poet, translator, and musician Haleh Liza Gafori describes the revered 13th-century Persian poet Rumi as “a good pal to humanity”. As she puts it, “He's rooting for our liberation.” In this exuberant conversation recorded for the 2025 Greenbelt Festival, she reads some of her translations, and she and Pádraig Ó Tuama illuminate the life of the man known as Rumi — his intense love of all things earthly and divine, the Islamic faith and universalist vision that flow through his work, and his life-changing connection with Shams, a Sufi mystic who catalyzed Rumi’s transformation from preacher to p
picks.reason: Discusses Rumi's Islamic-inspired poetry and universal spiritual themes of love and liberation.

picks.title: NEW SERIES: How to Be a Productive Muslim | #1 The Muslim's Guide to Getting More Out of Life #AMAU
picks.summary: You can be busy from morning to night and still not be productive. You can finish your work, answer messages, keep up with responsibilities, and still neglect what matters more. There is no shortage of books, systems and courses promising to help us do more, focus better and get more out of our time. But a Muslim has to ask a more important question first: productive for what? How to Be a Productive Muslim is a new series with Sheikh Muhammad Tim Humble حفظه الله looking at productivity through the Qur'an, Sunnah and guidance of the early Muslims. Not simply how to squeeze more into your day,
picks.reason: Considers productivity from an Islamic ethical perspective, questioning purpose beyond busyness.

picks.showTitle: Quran in a Year+ (with Imam Saif Morad)
picks.title: Day 338- Be Patient, But Don’t Be Passive | Ahkaf 33-35, Muhammad 1-11
picks.summary: in todays episode, we reflect on Allah’s command to the Prophet ﷺ to remain patient like the messengers of firm resolve and not to rush what Allah has not yet brought about.As we enter Surah Muḥammad, we explore how the Qur’an regulates even the most difficult human realities through revelation, authority, and the limits Allah has set. We also reflect on why Allah tests people through one another, why faith cannot be built upon following whoever appears strongest, and what it truly means to support the cause of Allah.
picks.reason: Reflects on patience, faith, and divine testing through Quranic stories and spiritual insight.

picks.title: Is Any Income Actually Halal Anymore? | Signs of the Hour Ep. 15 | Dr. Omar Suleiman
picks.summary: The Prophet ﷺ said he did not fear poverty for this ummah. He feared wealth, and he feared what abundance without barakah does to a community. A man would be handed a hundred dinars and still not be satisfied. People would stop asking where their money came from. One companion walked away from wealth that was even 10% doubtful. Find out why.Dr. Omar Suleiman traces the hadith of the end times about wealth in Signs of the Hour Ep. 15: greed placed in the hearts, the collapse of the question of halal income, and the narration that no one will be left untouched by riba.0:00 - Why the Prophet ﷺ fe
picks.reason: Analyzes hadith on wealth and ethics, focusing on spiritual dangers of greed and materialism.

picks.showTitle: Quran in a Year+ (with Imam Saif Morad)
picks.title: Day 337- The Danger of Misreading the Signs | Ahkaf 21-32
picks.summary: In today’s episode, we continue through Surah Al-Aḥqāf and the story of ʿĀd, a people blessed with strength, resources, hearing, sight, and intellect, yet none of it could save them when they rejected Allah’s guidance.We explore how our expectations can distort the way we see reality, why the Qur’an calls us to use our hearing, sight, and hearts properly, and what the jinn teach us about truly listening before we speak. We also reflect on the wisdom of Hūd عليه السلام in calling his people to Allah, and why even when our goal is right, the way we pursue it matters.
picks.reason: Explores Quranic story and spiritual lessons on perception, listening, and guidance.

picks.title: The Greatest Opening,What Is Surah Al-Fatihah
picks.summary: Surah Al-Fatihah is the first chapter of the Qur’an, the chapter that appears at the beginning of the Book of Allah and is present in the life of a Muslim every day.It is a surah that a Muslim hears during childhood, memorizes in youth, recites in every obligatory prayer, turns to in times of need, and keeps in the heart long after the Qur’an is closed.Though it contains only seven verses, its meaning reaches deeply into the foundations of Islamic faith.It speaks about Allah, His sovereignty, His mercy, His judgment, worship, dependence upon Him, guidance, righteousness, misguidance, accountab
picks.reason: Examines Surah Al-Fatihah's foundational spiritual meanings central to Islamic faith and practice.

picks.title: Could Surah Al-Ma'un Be Talking About You? | Surah al-Ma'un | Sheikh Mohamed Eid Almuhairi #AMAU
picks.summary: Reflect on Surah Al-Ma'un with Sheikh Mohamed Eid Almuhairi and uncover what it teaches about Salah, the Hereafter and how we treat people. ▶️ Watch more of this series on Tadabbur of the Qur'an: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQM1BksNs60k You may have memorised Surah Al-Ma'un. You may have recited it hundreds of times. But have you ever stopped to ask why Allah places these particular verses together? The Surah begins with the one who denies the Day of Recompense: someone harsh towards the orphan and unconcerned about the poor. Then comes a striking shift: "So woe to those who pray…"
picks.reason: Reflects deeply on Surah Al-Ma'un's ethical and spiritual lessons about faith and social conduct.

picks.title: AR-RAHMANIR-RAHIM,DISCOVERING THE VASTNESS OF ALLAH’S MERCY

picks.reason: Reflects on Allah's mercy as a vital spiritual concept beyond mere knowledge of power.
